title: Grammar: Tag Questions — Formation, Meaning, and Use
grammarTip:
Разделительные вопросы (Tag questions) — образование:

ОСНОВНОЕ ПРАВИЛО: обратная полярность!
Утверждение (+) → отрицательный тег: "She is a doctor, ISN'T she?"
Отрицание (–) → положительный тег: "You haven't met him, HAVE you?"

Схема по временам:
She works here, doesn't she?
They worked yesterday, didn't they?
He has finished, hasn't he?
You will come, won't you?
They are coming, aren't they?
She was there, wasn't she?

ОСОБЫЕ СЛУЧАИ:
"I am right, AREN'T I?" (не "amn't I")
"Let's go, SHALL WE?"
"Don't forget, WILL YOU?"
"Nobody came, DID THEY?" (nobody/nobody/everyone → they)

ИНТОНАЦИЯ:
↘ падающая = утверждение, ищу подтверждение
↗ растущая = настоящий вопрос, не уверен

grammarTable.subject: Positive → negative tag
grammarTable.verb: positive main clause + neg. auxiliary + pronoun
grammarTable.example: "She's a good listener, isn't she?" / "They've been practising, haven't they?"

grammarTable.subject: Negative → positive tag
grammarTable.verb: negative main clause + pos. auxiliary + pronoun
grammarTable.example: "He didn't prepare, did he?" / "They haven't tried this, have they?"

grammarTable.subject: With "be" as main verb
grammarTable.example: "The presentation was clear, wasn't it?" / "This is useful, isn't it?"

grammarTable.subject: With modal verbs
grammarTable.short: She can do it, can't she?
grammarTable.example: "You should slow down, shouldn't you?" / "They would help, wouldn't they?"

grammarTable.subject: With "have" (possession)
grammarTable.short: She has good posture, hasn't she?
grammarTable.example: "He has a lot of experience, hasn't he?" (BrE) / "He doesn't have..." (AmE)

grammarTable.subject: Imperative tags
grammarTable.example: "Let's try that again, shall we?" / "Don't be nervous, will you?" / "Listen carefully, will you?"

grammarExtra.title: The Two Main Functions of Tag Questions

rows.form: 1. Confirmation-seeking (falling intonation on tag): "I already know this — just confirm it"
rows.example: "You're an experienced speaker, aren't you?" ↘ (I think I know you are)

rows.form: 2. Genuine question (rising intonation on tag): "I'm not sure — please tell me"
rows.example: "You haven't done this before, have you?" ↗ (I genuinely don't know)

rows.form: 3. Softening a statement (falling intonation): making a comment sound less blunt
rows.example: "That was a bit fast, wasn't it?" ↘ (softer than "That was too fast")

rows.form: 4. Checking understanding (rising intonation): inviting confirmation in conversation
rows.example: "So the key point is clarity, is it?" ↗ (checking I understood correctly)

rows.form: Step 1: Identify the auxiliary in the main clause
rows.example: "She has been practising" → auxiliary: "has"

rows.form: Step 2: Reverse the polarity
rows.example: Positive "has" → negative tag "hasn't"; negative "hasn't" → positive "has"

rows.form: Step 3: Use the subject as a pronoun
rows.example: "She has been practising" → pronoun: "she" → tag: "hasn't she?"

rows.form: If there is no auxiliary: use do/does/did
rows.example: "You enjoy public speaking" → no auxiliary → "don't you?" / "You enjoyed it" → "didn't you?"

rows.form: "I am" → "aren't I?" (not "amn't I?" — rare in standard English)
rows.example: "I am right, aren't I?"

rows.form: "Nothing / nobody / nothing" → positive tag
rows.example: "Nothing works here, does it?" / "Nobody came, did they?"

rows.form: "Everyone/someone" → "they" as pronoun in tag
rows.example: "Everyone enjoyed the presentation, didn't they?"

rows.form: Negative words (hardly, never, rarely, barely) → positive tag
rows.example: "She barely speaks, does she?" / "He never prepares, does he?"

rows.form: Inviting agreement in conversation
rows.example: "It was a great presentation, wasn't it?" (expecting yes — falling intonation)

rows.form: Checking understanding after explaining
rows.example: "So the key is slowing down, right?" / "Does that make sense?" (rising intonation)

rows.form: Softening criticism or request
rows.example: "That was a bit long, wasn't it?" / "You could have slowed down, couldn't you?"

rows.form: Maintaining conversational flow
rows.example: "You've been to Japan, haven't you? So you know about high-context communication..."

rows.form: ❌ She is a good speaker, isn't he?
rows.example: ✅ She is a good speaker, isn't she? (tag pronoun must match subject)

rows.form: ❌ They arrived early, didn't it?
rows.example: ✅ They arrived early, didn't they? (use "they" not "it")

rows.form: ❌ You can speak French, can't he?
rows.example: ✅ You can speak French, can't you? (pronoun must match "you")

rows.form: ❌ She doesn't listen well, doesn't she?
rows.example: ✅ She doesn't listen well, does she? (negative → positive tag)

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct function of this tag question.
exercises.text: "The presentation was a bit fast, wasn't it?" ↘ (falling intonation)
opts: Genuine question — I don't know the answer
Softening a comment — I know it was fast
exercises.correct: Softening a comment — I know it was fast
exercises.hint: Falling intonation on the tag = I know the answer, making the comment softer

exercises.text: "She barely prepared for the talk, ___ ___?" (negative word "barely")

exercises.instruction: What function does this tag serve?
exercises.text: "You can hear me clearly in the back, can't you?" ↗ (rising intonation)
opts: Genuinely checking — I'm not sure if they can hear
exercises.correct: Genuinely checking — I'm not sure if they can hear
exercises.hint: Rising intonation = genuine question — I don't know the answer

questions.text: "She's been working on her communication skills, ___?" (tag)
questions.hint: Positive + present perfect "has been" → negative tag "hasn't she"
Negative past statement → positive tag "did he"

questions.text: "We should practise repair strategies more often, ___?" (modal tag)
"I'm getting better at presentations, ___ ___?" (special case: I am)
"Nobody in the room understood the accent, ___?"
"Let's try this activity, shall we?" uses the correct imperative tag.
questions.hint: "Let's" → "shall we?" is the correct imperative tag

questions.text: "She barely makes eye contact during presentations, ___ ___?" (negative word "barely")
A falling intonation on a tag question signals…
opts: A genuine question — I don't know the answer
Confirmation-seeking — I expect the answer I think is right
An invitation for the other person to speak at length
questions.correct: Confirmation-seeking — I expect the answer I think is right
questions.hint: Falling intonation = I already know the answer, just confirming

questions.text: "They can't improve without deliberate practice, ___ ___?" (negative modal)

opts: "She is a confident speaker, isn't she?"
"She is a good listener, doesn't she?"
questions.correct: "She is a good listener, doesn't she?"
questions.hint: "is" → "isn't she" — not "doesn't she" (only use "do" when there is no auxiliary)
